brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Four full hex bases form a 2x1 block on two levels: piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0 (storey 1) and piece:0,0,1, piece:1,0,1 (storey 2), joined by snap connectors. check_build reports meshClash clear and no errors.

requirements.requirement: For a workbench, at least two drawers
requirements.evidence: Three notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm at notch:0#0,1#notch1 on storey 1, hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf at notch:0#1,-1#notch4 on storey 1, and hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm at notch:1#0,1#notch1 on storey 2). Each sits in an empty cell between two touching bases, so the tower has 3 drawers, at least two as required.

The build is a compact 2-storey block of about 190 mm wide; it is a configurator-verified assembly, but no mounting or fixing to a bench was modelled (no bench-attachment part exists in the build), and load, material and strength are not assessed by the configurator.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey tower from four full hex bases with three notch drawers (two on storey 1, one on storey 2). The configurator reports no errors and a clear mesh check. Drawers were realised as notch drawer frames, since the half-base cut-face route offered no drawer sockets. Bench fixing and material/strength are not verified by the configurator.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
